source.description:
Reported by operator after running sp init --global from /home/dawid/dev/specialists/. Got 31 entries in ~/.config/specialists/user.json: 23 package canonical + 8 from this repo's .specialists/user/ (mercury-atomic-summarizer, official-document-analyzer, overthinker (overrides package), smoke-echo, squawk-event-curator, squawk-rolling-context, squawk-session-analyst, squawk-session-analyst-normalize).

Three concerns with the current behavior:

1. POLLUTION: in a different repo, those repo-local entries are inert — there's no matching package spec for them to override. They just sit there.

2. STICKINESS: the idempotency rule (C2: 'extends with newly-shipped specialists') only adds, never removes. Once a name is in user.json, it stays forever. Init from one repo permanently infects the global file.

3. CONCEPT MISMATCH: the global file's job is *cross-repo* defaults. Repo-specific specs belong in .specialists/user/<repo> and shouldn't ride in the cross-repo layer.

Proposed fix options:
(a) Restrict sp init --global to package canonical scope only (cleanest, least surprising)
(b) Prompt for each non-package spec ('include mercury-atomic-summarizer in global config? [y/N]')
(c) Add a --include-repo-overrides flag, default off

The current C2 implementation uses SpecialistLoader.list() directly (src/cli/init.ts, src/specialist/global-config.ts). The fix is to filter by scope='package' before generating the template entries.
source.title: sp init --global should not bake repo-local .specialists/user/ specs into the global file
